title: The Torah and Its Rules
bigQuestion: Why does a rule from the Torah need so many questions?

story.title: Is Coloring Work?
story.kicker: One short rule from the Torah starts a big argument in Room 12.
paragraphs: Ms. Ortiz read a rule to the class. "The Torah says: rest on the seventh day. Do no work." She put down the book. "What counts as work?" she asked.
Hands went up. "Digging is work," said Leo. "Cooking is work," said Priya. Then Mia asked, "Is coloring work?" The room went quiet. Then everyone talked at once.
"Coloring is fun, so it is not work," said Leo. "But you make something new," said Priya. "Making things is work." Mia was not sure. "What if I color for school?" she asked.
Ms. Ortiz smiled. "Long ago, rabbis asked this same kind of question. They filled many books with their answers. That set of books is the Talmud."
story.think: Do you think coloring is work? What would make it work or not work?

lessons.title: Five Books on a Scroll
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah is the first five books of the Bible, kept as a long scroll.
reading: The *Torah* is the first five books of the Bible. The first book is Genesis. The last book is Deuteronomy. Together they are one long story with many rules.
In a synagogue, the Torah is kept as a scroll. A scroll is a long roll of paper or animal skin. It has two wooden rods. You roll it to find your place.
Every week, Jewish people read a part of the Torah out loud. By the end of the year, they finish all five books. Then they start again.

words.d: the first five books of the Bible, kept as a scroll
a long roll of writing on two wooden rods

look.title: A Scroll in Words
look.text: Picture a long roll of tan skin. It is wrapped around two wooden rods. The writing is in Hebrew, in neat black columns. To read the next part, you roll one rod and unroll the other. The scroll is heavy. Two people carry it.
look.prompt: How is a scroll different from the books in your classroom?

check.q: What is the Torah?
choices: The first five books of the Bible
check.why: The Torah is the first five books of the Bible, from Genesis to Deuteronomy.

check.q: How is the Torah kept in a synagogue?
check.why: The Torah is kept as a long scroll on two wooden rods.

check.q: How often do Jewish people finish reading the whole Torah?
check.why: A part is read each week, and the whole Torah is finished in a year.

lessons.title: Moses on the Mountain
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish tradition says Moses received the Torah at Mount Sinai.
reading: Jewish tradition says the Torah came from God. It says Moses received it at *Mount Sinai*. Mount Sinai is a mountain in a desert.
The Torah tells the story. The people camp at the foot of the mountain. Moses goes up. He comes down with rules for the people to keep.
Different people read this story in different ways. Some read it as history. Some read it as a holy story. In this class, we say what the Torah tells and what tradition holds.

words.d: the mountain where, Jewish tradition says, Moses received the Torah

look.title: A Rule From the Mountain
look.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
look.prompt: What does this rule ask people to do? What word is new to you?

check.q: Where does Jewish tradition say Moses received the Torah?
check.why: Jewish tradition says Moses received the Torah at Mount Sinai.

check.q: In the Torah's story, who goes up the mountain?
check.why: The Torah tells that Moses went up Mount Sinai. Akiva and Rashi lived much later.

check.q: What does this class say about the Sinai story?
choices: What the Torah tells and what tradition holds
check.why: We describe what the text says and how people read it, without deciding for anyone.

lessons.title: What a Mitzvah Is
lessons.mainIdea: A rule in the Torah is called a mitzvah.
reading: A rule in the Torah is called a *mitzvah*. More than one are called mitzvot. Some mitzvot say, "Do this." Some say, "Do not do this."
Here are some mitzvot. Honor your father and mother. Do not steal. Leave some of your crops for poor people. Rest on the seventh day.
Rabbinic tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah. That is a lot of rules! Many of them are about being fair and kind to other people.

words.d: a rule in the Torah; more than one are mitzvot

look.title: Counting the Rules
look.cite: Rabbinic tradition's count, given in the Babylonian Talmud, Makkot 23b
look.prompt: Are there more Do rules or more Do not rules?

check.q: What is a mitzvah?
check.why: A mitzvah is a rule in the Torah. More than one are mitzvot.

check.q: How many mitzvot does rabbinic tradition count?
check.why: Rabbinic tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah.

check.q: Which of these is a mitzvah from the Torah?
check.why: Honor your father and mother is a rule in the Torah. The others are ways people study.

lessons.title: Shabbat, the Seventh Day
lessons.mainIdea: Shabbat is a day of rest that comes every week on the seventh day.
reading: *Shabbat* is the seventh day of the week. The Torah says to work six days and rest on the seventh. Shabbat starts Friday at sunset. It ends Saturday night.
Many Jewish families light candles on Friday evening. They eat a special meal. They sing. They do not go to work or school. It is a day to rest and be together.
The Torah says everyone rests. Parents rest. Children rest. Helpers rest. Even the animals rest. Rabbinic tradition says Shabbat is a gift.

words.d: the seventh day of the week, a day of rest from Friday sunset to Saturday night

look.title: Work Days and Rest Days
look.prompt: How many more work days are there than rest days?

check.q: When does Shabbat begin?
check.why: Shabbat begins Friday at sunset and ends Saturday night.

check.q: Who rests on Shabbat, according to the Torah?
check.why: The Torah says parents, children, helpers, and even animals rest.

check.q: What do many Jewish families do on Friday evening?
choices: Light candles and eat a special meal
check.why: Many families light candles, eat together, and sing on Friday evening.

lessons.title: A Rule Needs Explaining
lessons.mainIdea: A short rule like "do no work" makes people ask what work means.
reading: The Torah says, "Do no work on Shabbat." That sounds simple. But what is work? Is carrying a bag work? Is writing work? Is lighting a lamp work?
The Torah does not give a list. So people asked. The *Mishnah* gave an answer. It listed thirty-nine kinds of work. Planting is one. Cooking is one. Writing is one.
A rule can be short. Living by it takes more words. That is why a short rule can lead to a very long book.

words.d: the short, old teaching that lists rules, like the thirty-nine kinds of work

look.title: Forty Less One
look.text: The Mishnah lists the kinds of work not done on Shabbat. It calls them forty less one. The list starts with planting and plowing. It has baking, weaving, tying a knot, and writing two letters. It ends with carrying something from one place to another.
look.cite: Mishnah Shabbat 7:2, retold in simple words
look.prompt: Pick one kind of work from the list. Why might the rabbis have called it work?

check.q: Why did people ask what work means?
choices: The Torah gives a long list
The Torah's rule is short and does not list kinds of work
No one cared about the rule
check.why: The Torah says do no work but does not list what work is, so people asked.

check.q: How many kinds of work does the Mishnah list?
check.why: The Mishnah lists thirty-nine kinds of work, called forty less one.

check.q: Which of these is on the Mishnah's list?
check.why: Writing two letters is one of the thirty-nine kinds of work in Mishnah Shabbat 7:2.

lessons.title: The Rabbis Worked It Out
lessons.mainIdea: The Talmud is where the rabbis asked and answered questions about the rules.
reading: The Mishnah gave a list. But the list made new questions. What if you carry something small? What if you write one letter, not two? The rabbis asked all of this.
Their questions and answers were written down. That is the *Gemara*. The Mishnah and the Gemara together are the Talmud. Rule, question, answer, new question.
The rabbis cared about people. They asked: what if someone is sick on Shabbat? They said saving a life comes first. A rule about rest should not hurt anyone.

words.d: the rabbis' questions and answers about the Mishnah

look.title: A Life Comes First
look.text: The Talmud teaches that if someone's life is in danger on Shabbat, you do what is needed to save them. The rabbis say Shabbat was given to people, not people to Shabbat. Saving a life sets the Shabbat rules aside.
look.cite: Babylonian Talmud, Yoma 85b, retold in simple words
look.prompt: What does this rule protect? Why might the rabbis have put it first?

check.q: What is the Gemara?
choices: The first five books of the Bible
The rabbis' questions and answers about the Mishnah
check.why: The Gemara is the rabbis' talk about the Mishnah. Together they make the Talmud.

check.q: What did the rabbis say if someone's life is in danger on Shabbat?
check.why: The Talmud in Yoma 85b says saving a life comes before the Shabbat rules.

check.q: What two parts make up the Talmud?
check.why: The Mishnah and the Gemara together are the Talmud.

lessons.title: A Good Question Is Learning
lessons.mainIdea: Asking a good question is a way of learning.
reading: The rabbis loved questions. A question is not a mistake. A question shows you are thinking. In the Talmud, a good question is praised.
Pirkei Avot is a small book of rabbis' sayings. It says a shy person does not learn. That means: if you are afraid to ask, you miss out. So ask!
In this class, you can ask anything about the Talmud. What does that word mean? Why did they say that? Every question helps us learn.

words.d: a small book of rabbis' sayings, part of the Mishnah

look.title: Do Not Be Too Shy to Ask
look.text: In Pirkei Avot, Hillel says that a shy person cannot learn, and a quick-tempered person cannot teach.
look.cite: Mishnah Avot 2:5, retold from Charles Taylor, Sayings of the Jewish Fathers (1877)
look.prompt: Why would being shy make it hard to learn? Why would a bad temper make it hard to teach?

check.q: What do the rabbis think about a good question?
check.why: In the Talmud, a good question is praised. It shows thinking.

check.q: What is Pirkei Avot?
check.why: Pirkei Avot is a small book of rabbis' sayings inside the Mishnah.

check.q: What does Hillel say about a shy person?
choices: A shy person rests on Shabbat
check.why: Avot 2:5 says a shy person cannot learn, because they do not ask.

choices: The first five books of the Bible
review.why: The Torah is the first five books of the Bible, kept as a scroll.

review.q: A rule in the Torah is called what?
review.why: A mitzvah is a rule in the Torah. A daf is a page and a chavruta is a partner.
Shabbat is the seventh day, a day of rest.

review.q: Why did the rule "do no work" lead to many questions?
choices: It does not say what work is

review.q: Where did the rabbis write down their questions and answers?
review.why: The rabbis' questions and answers are in the Talmud, in the Gemara.

review.q: What did the rabbis say comes first, even on Shabbat?
review.why: Yoma 85b says saving a life sets the Shabbat rules aside.
